verifier_note: Checked all 55 unique warrant sources by retrieval (WebFetch, near-verbatim quote match against every claim sentence), ran all 48 checks[] myself through the real oracle (python scripts/compile_oracle.py check, rustc 1.98.1 + rapier3d-f64 0.35.3/enhanced-determinism) with 48/48 passing their exact expect/stdout/error_codes/lints metadata, and verified every engine_note against si-rpg-engine at origin/main via gh api (solver/src/lib.rs, solver/src/rapier_law.rs, solver/Cargo.toml, solver/rust-toolchain.toml, commit history for 4782a8a and 2c2631f, and docs/dispatch-t2-restore.md for the T2/solver_restore reference). No source was unfindable, no API or lint name was wrong, no check tested a different claim than its prose, and no engine fact was wrong; one non-obvious detail (parry3d-f64's Vector coming from glam DVec3 'via glamx') was independently confirmed true rather than assumed. The lane's one systemic weakness is citation hygiene, not content: the ordered-float source uses an unpinned docs.rs '/latest/' URL (every other external-crate citation in the lane is version-pinned), so a future ordered-float release could silently change what that link shows even though it is accurate today; a second, softer weakness is that several 'what/how' claims about docs.rs-hosted external crates (rapier3d-f64, parry3d-f64, glam) depend on those third-party pages staying live at their pinned versions rather than on Rust's own infrastructure.
